All three versions are working. They're identical except for **how you add a tag** — please open each one, add a couple of tags and a short note to any link, and notice which way of adding tags feels most natural to you.

In each version: find a link, click **"＋ Add tags & note"**, add some tags and a note, then press **Save**.

- **Version A** — http://maker:4001/tags.html?mode=chips
  You type a tag and press **Enter**; each tag turns into a little removable chip. Good for adding them one at a time.

- **Version B** — http://maker:4001/tags.html?mode=text
  You type **all your tags in one box, separated by commas**. Fast if you like typing them in one go.

- **Version C** — http://maker:4001/tags.html?mode=picker
  You **click to pick from tags you've used before**, and can add a new one. Helps you reuse the same tags instead of inventing slight variations.

A couple of things I set up that apply to all three — please check these too:

- **Notes** are a simple free-text box under the tags; I've assumed one note per link. Let me know if that fits what you pictured.
- **Tags and notes are both searchable** — try saving a tag, then type it into the search box up top. I extended search to cover them (this includes the note-searchability you asked for; tags I added on the same basis — tell me if you'd *not* want tags searchable).

Tell me which tag-adding version feels right (it's fine to mix — e.g. "A but I'd also want C's reuse"), and how the notes feel.
